records.stem: At a Massachusetts pharmacy, a fentanyl prescription from a Rhode Island practitioner was issued four days ago and the pharmacist obtains direct verification. What Massachusetts rule is central?

choices.text: Use the 30-day out-of-state Schedule III-through-VI window.
Fill any state's Schedule II narcotic prescription within five days.
Skip direct verification because Rhode Island is contiguous.
Treat electronic transmission as resetting the five-day issue period.
Apply the contiguous-state Schedule II narcotic pathway and its five-day and verification conditions.

records.stem: On Friday morning, a pharmacy discovers a significant unexplained loss of controlled substances. The investigation cannot be completed that day. Which federal response is correct?

choices.text: Wait for the investigation before contacting DEA.
Give oral notice within 24 hours and take no further action.
File Form 106 within one business day instead of separate notice.
Send written DEA notice within one business day and Form 106 within 45 calendar days.
Notify only the Massachusetts Board because the loss occurred in Massachusetts.

records.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a warfarin prescription issued 20 days ago by a Rhode Island practitioner who is properly licensed and registered as required. Massachusetts treats warfarin as Schedule VI. The pharmacist independently judges the prescription to be authentic and valid. A colleague says Massachusetts nevertheless requires separate telephone verification of every out-of-state Schedule III through VI prescription. What is the best response?

choices.text: The colleague is correct because the separate verification mandate applies identically to Schedules III, IV, V, and VI whenever a prescription was issued outside Massachusetts.
The prescription is barred because any out-of-state Schedule VI prescription must be filled within 7 days.
The prescription may be considered within the 30-day III-VI window if judged authentic and valid; separate prescriber verification applies to Schedules III-V, not Schedule VI.
Schedule VI prescriptions from another state require no pharmacist authenticity or validity judgment.
The prescription becomes a federal Schedule V prescription when presented across state lines, so the Schedule III-V verification rule applies.

records.stem:
Case A: A confirmed reportable breach of unsecured PHI affects 20 individuals, and the pharmacy proposes waiting until the annual HHS report to notify those individuals.

Case B: A manager treats the 60-day outer limit as an automatic permission to wait the full period even though earlier notice is feasible; no authorized delay applies.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The small-breach annual HHS route does not postpone the individual-notification obligation.
The small-breach HHS deadline is within 60 days after the discovery calendar year ends.
Notice must be provided without unreasonable delay, not routinely held until the outer limit.
One regulator filing necessarily serves as notice to all affected individuals.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Individual and regulator notifications have different recipients and may have different clocks.
Notice must be provided without unreasonable delay, not routinely held until the outer limit.

choices.text: The small-breach HHS clock starts 60 days after each affected patient next visits.
A breach affecting fewer than 500 people permits individual notice to wait for the annual HHS report.
Notice must be provided without unreasonable delay, not routinely held until the outer limit.
One regulator filing necessarily serves as notice to all affected individuals.

records.stem:
A pharmacist has continuously practiced under a Rhode Island license but allowed an unrestricted Massachusetts registration to lapse for two years and three months. There was no suspension, revocation, or military-service extension. The pharmacist now seeks Massachusetts renewal.

Which examination requirement is expressly part of this renewal pathway? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: No Massachusetts examination is needed because the Rhode Island license stayed current.
Passing MPJE is required, together with any other conditions set by the Board.
Both NAPLEX and MPJE are mandatory before renewal after this ordinary lapse.
Additional CE is the stated substitute for MPJE once the back fees are paid.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy receives a microbiology report showing an action-level result, but personnel plan to delay Board notification until final organism identification is complete.

Case B: The same ISO area has another action-level finding within 60 days, separated from the first by an acceptable result.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: MOR, designated PIC, or the specified pharmacist designee follows the applicable reporting role.
An acceptable result between two findings necessarily prevents the described repeat-within-60-days trigger.
Organism identification, location history, and trends remain relevant to investigation.
The described one-business-day notification clock runs from microbiology-report receipt without waiting for later identification.

records.stem:
A Massachusetts resident Drug Store pharmacy will close permanently on November 30. It has no Board authorization to vary the usual closure-notice requirements. A patient last had a prescription filled at this pharmacy on September 20, has no refills remaining, and has no prescription awaiting pickup. The manager proposes excluding this patient from individual notices and relying on a sign in the pharmacy.

How should the pharmacy handle notice to this patient? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Attempt individual notice by November 16, using first-class mail or another Board-approved method.
Exclude the patient because the prescription has no remaining refills and nothing awaits pickup.
Use the posted closure sign as this patient's notice because no prescription transfer is pending.
Send the patient's notice by December 14 with the pharmacy's post-closure license documents.

records.stem: A pharmacist discovers that the wrong strength was dispensed yesterday and the patient may still be taking it. What is the immediate priority?

choices.text: Finish the root-cause analysis before contacting the patient.
Notify the patient, give harm-minimization directions, and contact the prescriber as professional judgment requires.
Notify only the prescriber and wait for instructions before contacting the patient.
Document within 24 hours but defer corrective directions until then.
Report every QRE to the Board before assisting the patient.

records.stem: At prescription intake, a resident pharmacy plans to close in 10 days and has not notified the Board. What timing problem exists?

choices.text: Ten days is enough when the pharmacy posts a sign immediately.
The ordinary rule calls for certified written Board notice at least 14 days before closure.
Notify the Board within 14 days after closure instead.
Use ordinary email rather than the required certified written notice.
Wait until the final prescription is transferred before announcing the date.

records.stem: A pharmacist discovers a dispensing error while the patient may still be exposed to harm. Which duties apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Immediately notify the patient or representative and give correction and harm-minimization directions.
Finish root-cause analysis before contacting the patient.
Always notify the patient before the prescriber in a strict sequence.
Immediately notify the prescriber when professional judgment indicates it is warranted.
Complete the initial QRE documentation within 24 hours after discovery or notification.

records.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee has now worked 1520 hours over ten months. Which statements correctly describe the trainee employment limit? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The limit is 1500 hours or one year, whichever period is shorter.
The Board may grant an extension beyond the limit.
The limit does not yet apply if the individual has not reached 18 years of age.
The limit is suspended whenever the employing pharmacy is short staffed.
An individual who exceeded the limit before turning 18 must apply for a technician licence within 30 days of the 18th birthday.

records.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist discloses nothing about any patient to anyone. Completed prescriptions sit face up on an open counter and a printed waiting list showing patient names is visible to everyone standing in the queue. No one is shown to have read either of them. What is the position?

choices.text: Compliant, because the pharmacist made no disclosure to any third party.
Compliant, because no one is shown to have read the information on display.
Compliant, provided the pharmacy makes a private consultation area available.
In breach, but only once a patient complains about the arrangement.
In breach, because the duty includes protecting confidential information.

records.stem: At one Massachusetts pharmacy a patient refuses to give any allergy history after being asked on three separate visits. At another, a patient is never asked because the queue is long. Both patient profiles are incomplete in exactly the same respect. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Both pharmacies are compliant, because the standard is only reasonable effort.
Both pharmacies are in breach, because the profile has to be complete.
Compliance turns on whether the missing history was clinically significant.
The first pharmacy made a reasonable effort and is compliant on these facts.
The second pharmacy made no effort at all and is not compliant.

records.stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist holds a Department registration for the purpose of prescribing and a valid agreement. She wishes to dispense a Schedule VI product for immediate treatment. That particular product is not among those her agreement authorises her to prescribe. May she do so?

choices.text: Yes, because immediate treatment is a separate power from prescribing.
Yes, because the product sits in Schedule VI, the least restricted schedule.
Yes, provided she notifies the supervising physician within 24 hours.
No, because the power runs only to substances she is authorised to prescribe.
No, because dispensing for immediate treatment requires a patient-specific order.

records.stem:
Case A: After an eligible medication injection, the patient requires additional treatment and monitoring in an emergency department; staff plan to wait 24 hours before notifying the prescriber.

Case B: A nonserious reaction in another patient is discussed under the circular's recommendation for communication within 24 hours.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Calling the prescriber completes every otherwise applicable Board reporting duty.
The serious outcome requires immediate prescriber notification rather than waiting for the routine interval.
Completing the report takes priority over necessary emergency care.
The circular uses the same mandatory 24-hour deadline for serious and nonserious reactions.

records.stem:
Case A: After an eligible medication injection, the patient requires additional treatment and monitoring in an emergency department; staff plan to wait 24 hours before notifying the prescriber.

Case B: A nonserious reaction in another patient is discussed under the circular's recommendation for communication within 24 hours.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A prescriber call does not replace a separately triggered Board report for an error or serious event.
The serious outcome requires immediate prescriber notification rather than waiting for the routine interval.
Emergency care must not be delayed while staff finish the report.

records.stem:
Case A: A medication bag containing another patient's identifiable information is handed to the wrong person; staff conclude that an accidental disclosure cannot be a breach.

Case B: The pharmacy retrieves the bag and assumes retrieval alone proves that no information was seen or compromised.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Recovering the bag conclusively proves no information was viewed.
An undocumented assurance that nobody was harmed replaces assessment of compromise.
An impermissible disclosure is evaluated under the breach framework even if the act was accidental.
Opening a CQI record automatically completes all privacy breach analysis.

records.stem:
Case A: A reportable unsecured-PHI breach affects exactly 500 individuals, all residing in one state; no other media-notice trigger is present.

Case B: A separate breach affects 501 residents of one state.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The first breach meets the 500-or-more threshold for the specified HHS reporting route.
A required media notice replaces the individual notices.
The second breach fails the media threshold because 501 is not more than 500.
The first breach meets the more-than-500 media threshold solely because exactly 500 residents are affected.

choices.text: A required media notice replaces the individual notices.
The second breach meets the more-than-500-residents threshold for the specified media notice.
The first breach falls into the fewer-than-500 annual HHS route.
The first breach meets the more-than-500 media threshold solely because exactly 500 residents are affected.

records.stem:
Case A: During a system outage, a pharmacy proposes bypassing identity checks and duplicate-dispensing controls because electronic access is unavailable.

Case B: After discovering a suspected security incident, staff delete the relevant logs before investigating, calling this cleanup.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: An outage does not create a general exemption from identity and duplicate-dispensing safeguards.
Incident response should preserve relevant evidence rather than erase the logs needed for investigation.
A suspected incident must be assessed for the applicable breach and other reporting triggers.
Restoration should include reconciliation of appropriate downtime records.

records.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist reviews outpatient labels and proposed substitutions. Assume the prescriber’s intended ingredient, strength, dosage form, and route are known. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which ONE proposed handling is supported by the applicable requirements?

choices.text: During a qualifying medical emergency, a pharmacist uses verbal purchaser agreement alone for the permitted substitution despite the required written acceptance.
A pharmacist changes an immediate-release prescription to an extended-release product with the same ingredient and strength without clarification.
A pharmacist gives a reconstituted medication a one-year label date without considering its shorter in-use limit.
A pharmacist gives the patient the required written notification after an eligible biological substitution.

records.stem:
An emergency meeting the applicable requirements justifies an oral CII authorization. The prescriber requests only the amount adequate to treat the patient during the emergency period.

Which statements reflect the federal emergency pathway? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist immediately records the required oral-prescription information.
The pharmacist can independently increase the quantity to a standard monthly supply.
A central-fill pharmacy may use this oral route to prepare the CII order.
The emergency quantity is limited to the amount adequate for the emergency period.
Failure to obtain the required follow-up triggers the pharmacist's DEA-notification duty.

records.stem: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy is drafting the operating procedure for a new central-fill arrangement with a second pharmacy. The draft has to state where each finished prescription goes and what work the central site may perform. Which statements are correct under current Board policy? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A centrally filled Schedule IV prescription must go to the pharmacy where the prescription originated for final dispensing to the patient.
A centrally filled Schedule VI prescription that does not require Prescription Monitoring Program reporting may be shipped directly to the patient by the central fill pharmacy.
A centrally filled Schedule VI prescription for a drug that does require Prescription Monitoring Program reporting may also be shipped directly to the patient, since it is not federally scheduled.
A central fill pharmacy sited outside Massachusetts does not need its own Massachusetts pharmacy license while the originating pharmacy holds one.
Central filling of compounded sterile preparations for dispensing within Massachusetts is not permitted.

records.stem: A pharmacy mailed an executed paper DEA Form 222 to its supplier. The supplier reports that the form never arrived, no Schedule II goods were shipped, and the pharmacy cannot locate the original. The pharmacy still needs the order. What is the appropriate federal replacement process?

choices.text: Send the supplier a photocopy of the lost form and ask it to treat the photocopy as the original order.
Execute a new Form 222, attach the required statement identifying the lost form and nonreceipt of goods, retain the required copies, and make the applicable DEA loss report.
Ask the supplier to recreate the purchaser's lost form because only suppliers may issue replacement Form 222s.
Wait 60 days from the lost form's execution date; only after expiration may a replacement order be issued.
Treat the missing paper form as an inventory significant loss and file only DEA Form 106 without replacing the order.

records.stem:
A retail pharmacy sends prescription processing to an authorized central-fill pharmacy. The patient will collect the finished prescription at the retail pharmacy. A manager calls this a patient-requested refill transfer and closes the retail record without preserving the shared-service linkage.

Which correction is appropriate? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Keep the retail/central-fill roles linked in the required shared-service records.
Keep only the shipping label because the finished product returns to retail.
Restart the prescription's validity period when central fill receives it.
Treat the central-fill pharmacy as the patient's prescriber.

records.stem:
Case A: For a proposed federal emergency oral Schedule II prescription, the prescriber's receptionist calls a certified technician instead of the prescribing practitioner speaking to the pharmacist.

Case B: A central-fill pharmacy proposes accepting the emergency oral prescription directly under the ordinary retail emergency pathway.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The federal emergency-oral provision does not allow the central-fill pharmacy to receive it through that pathway.
The specified federal emergency pathway requires the prescribing individual practitioner to authorize the pharmacist.
An unknown caller's assertion of being a prescriber removes the need for authenticity verification.
The pharmacist must promptly reduce the required oral information to a record.

records.stem:

Case B: A central-fill pharmacy proposes accepting the emergency oral prescription directly under the ordinary retail emergency pathway.

choices.text: An unknown caller's assertion of being a prescriber removes the need for authenticity verification.

The pharmacist must promptly reduce the required oral information to a record.
The federal emergency-oral provision does not allow the central-fill pharmacy to receive it through that pathway.

records.stem:
A resident Board-licensed Massachusetts pharmacy evaluates the following event under Policy 2026-01. A single Schedule VI tablet was confirmed stolen by an employee. This question concerns the Board loss-reporting pathway only, not whether a separate federal notice is required.

Which response follows the stated Board policy? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Handle the confirmed dispensing error through CQI; this policy does not require a loss report for that error.
Document the investigated insignificant loss on site and monitor adverse trends.
Continue the investigation; do not submit an unconfirmed loss as a confirmed Board loss.
Submit the Board’s confirmed-loss report within 7 calendar days, including DEA Form 106 if applicable.

records.stem:
A pharmacy purchases or transfers controlled stock between registrants. These are stock transactions, not patient prescription-information transfers. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacy distinguishes DEA Form 106 loss reporting from Form 222 ordering and Form 41 destruction records.
A pharmacy calculates the practitioner-distribution exception using applicable controlled-substance dosage units.
A pharmacy checks both the recipient’s registration and the required ordering records before an eligible controlled-stock transfer.
A supplier restarts a 60-day completion period with each partial shipment on the same Form 222.
An eligible Schedule II stock purchase uses a properly executed Form 222 or qualifying CSOS order.

records.stem: During closing procedures, a Massachusetts pharmacy discovers that its controlled-substance storage cabinet no longer locks. The inventory reconciles and no theft or loss is known. A technician suggests leaving the controlled stock there overnight because the alarm system covers the building. What is the best response?

choices.text: Leave the stock in place because a theft report is required only after an actual loss is proved.
Move or otherwise secure the controlled stock under compliant restricted-access conditions before closing and address the failed security control.
Convert all controlled stock to will-call prescriptions so the cabinet no longer contains pharmacy inventory.
Wait until the next biennial inventory to determine whether the broken lock caused a reportable discrepancy.
File DEA Form 106 immediately even though no theft or significant loss has been discovered.

records.stem: A pharmacy has already mailed a valid paper DEA Form 222 to its supplier for three Schedule II products. Before shipment, the pharmacy decides it no longer needs one line item but wants the other two. What is the appropriate federal way to stop that portion of the order?

choices.text: Send the supplier written cancellation of the identified line; the supplier documents the cancellation on the original Form 222.
Ask the supplier to erase the unwanted line from the executed original form before filling the remaining lines.
File DEA Form 106 for the unwanted line because canceling an order is treated as a significant loss.
Cancel the entire pharmacy DEA registration because a submitted Form 222 cannot be changed in part.
Wait for delivery, accept the unwanted Schedule II product, and destroy it because pre-shipment cancellation is prohibited.

records.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy plans to mail a temperature-sensitive prescription using a common carrier. The proposed packaging cannot reasonably maintain the product's labeled storage conditions during the expected transit. What should the pharmacy do?

choices.text: Ship it because use of a common carrier transfers responsibility for product stability to the carrier.
Ship it if the patient agrees to accept the risk of temperature excursion.
Use a packing and transportation method that protects medication integrity and stability before sending the prescription.
Remove the labeled storage directions so the carrier is not responsible for them.
Convert the order to an in-store pickup without telling the patient.

records.stem: Two separately owned Massachusetts pharmacies want one pharmacy to perform central-fill services for prescriptions originating at the other. They have compatible secure systems but no common ownership. Which governance step is central to making this shared-service structure permissible under current Board policy?

choices.text: They must become commonly owned because unrelated pharmacies may not participate in shared pharmacy services.
They should use a written agreement that defines the shared services and each participating pharmacy's responsibilities, while satisfying the policy's other safeguards.
They may proceed without an agreement if both Managers of Record give oral approval.
They should transfer every prescription to the filling pharmacy and stop treating the arrangement as central fill.
They need a patient-specific court order for each prescription processed through the arrangement.

records.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives filled and labelled vials from a central facility in another state that is not licensed by the Board. On arrival the pharmacist inspects each vial against the prescription and finds everything correct. May the pharmacy dispense them?

choices.text: Yes, because the pharmacist has personally checked each finished product.
Yes, because central fill is a recognised part of ordinary pharmacy practice.
No, unless the process was verified by a Massachusetts licensed pharmacist.
No, because a pharmacy may never dispense what it did not process itself.
No, unless the receiving pharmacy documents the inspection in the patient profile.

records.stem:
Case A: An RTS container may contain a recalled lot, but the pharmacy cannot confirm that it is outside the recall.

Case B: A delivery is returned after an uncertain temperature history, and staff assume the sealed outer package proves the product remained suitable.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Any carrier loss makes all investigation and applicable reporting solely the carrier's responsibility.
Every returned package has the same legal custody and reuse status.
Sealed outer packaging conclusively proves acceptable temperature history.
The potentially affected RTS medicine cannot be re-dispensed until the pharmacy confirms it is not within the recalled lot.

Case B: A delivery is returned after an uncertain temperature history, and staff assume the sealed outer package proves the product remained suitable.

choices.text: An intact outer package does not by itself establish acceptable temperature exposure and product integrity.
Uncertain lot identity permits dispensing if the container was originally filled before the recall notice.

Case B: A central-fill pharmacy proposes accepting the emergency oral prescription directly under the ordinary retail emergency pathway.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The pharmacist may dispense first and postpone all oral-order recording until the follow-up arrives.
A central-fill pharmacy may accept the emergency oral Schedule II order through the same retail pathway.
The specified federal emergency pathway requires the prescribing individual practitioner to authorize the pharmacist.
An unknown caller's assertion of being a prescriber removes the need for authenticity verification.

records.stem:
Case A: For a proposed federal emergency oral Schedule II prescription, the prescriber's receptionist calls a certified technician instead of the prescribing practitioner speaking to the pharmacist.

Case B: A central-fill pharmacy proposes accepting the emergency oral prescription directly under the ordinary retail emergency pathway.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The receptionist-to-technician call satisfies that specific emergency authorization pathway.
The pharmacist may dispense first and postpone all oral-order recording until the follow-up arrives.
An unknown caller's assertion of being a prescriber removes the need for authenticity verification.
The federal emergency-oral provision does not allow the central-fill pharmacy to receive it through that pathway.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy uses DEA Form 106 as though it were the ordering document for an ordinary Schedule II stock purchase.

Case B: The pharmacy returns eligible Schedule II stock to an authorized supplier and assumes the return eliminates all applicable ordering and transaction records.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A return to the supplier is exempt from all Schedule II transaction documentation.
Expiration removes the controlled status and all inventory responsibility immediately.
Any patient return can be processed as a registrant-to-supplier stock purchase reversal.
The applicable Form 222 or CSOS ordering pathway is distinct from the Form 106 loss report.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy uses DEA Form 106 as though it were the ordering document for an ordinary Schedule II stock purchase.

Case B: The pharmacy returns eligible Schedule II stock to an authorized supplier and assumes the return eliminates all applicable ordering and transaction records.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A patient return is not the same as a registrant's stock return.
Expiration removes the controlled status and all inventory responsibility immediately.
A registrant stock return must follow its applicable Part 1305 and transaction-record requirements.
The applicable Form 222 or CSOS ordering pathway is distinct from the Form 106 loss report.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy discovers a reportable theft and plans to withhold the initial written DEA notice until a final quantity investigation is complete.

Case B: Staff confuse the current provision's completed electronic Form 106 period with the separate initial-notice deadline.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A confirmed theft needs no report whenever only a small quantity was taken.
Only losses above a universal fixed dollar threshold can be significant under the described rule.
The applicable initial written DEA notice is due within one business day of discovery.
